title: Canonical dense-lattice restriction on trivial representations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, a finite intermediate field $E$, and $F\in\{E,\Omega\}$. Put $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ on the coherent profinite site, with all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Let $r\geq0$, let $L=\mathbf Z_\ell^r$ with its inverse-limit topology and $D=\mathbf Z^r$ with the discrete topology, and let $\iota:D\to L$ be the coordinatewise integer inclusion. Let $W$ be any finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space with trivial $L$-action [def-pod-l-adic-representations]. Set $W_F(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E W)$, with the finite-dimensional product norm topology on $F\otimes_E W$ and trivial action. Use internal $C_F$-modules with condensed group actions [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and ordinary total right derived invariants in their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The canonical derived restriction morphism induced by invariant inclusion, normalized as in [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus],
$$b_F(W):R\Gamma_L(W_F[0])\longrightarrow R\Gamma_D(\operatorname{Res}_\iota W_F[0]),$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$. This includes $W=0$ and $r=0$ and uses the norm topology on the possibly noncomplete $F=\Omega$.

proof.text: Put $R=C_F$. For scalar coefficients, [lem-sfb-trivial-ladic-derived-exterior] gives an isomorphism $\chi_L:\mathcal E_{R,r}\to R\Gamma_L(R[0])$, whose summand $I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}$ is the ordered cup of the positive coordinate classes $\alpha_i$ (the empty summand is the unit). Apply [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-cup-exterior] to this same commutative condensed ring $R$: it gives an isomorphism $\chi_D:\mathcal E_{R,r}\to R\Gamma_D(R[0])$ with summands the ordered cups of the integer-coordinate classes $\delta_i$. Both statements specify actual derived morphisms, with the same zero-differential finite-sum source.

proof.text: Let $b=b_\iota(R)$ be the invariant-inclusion-normalized restriction. The calculus [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] gives $b\alpha_i=[a_i\circ\iota]=\delta_i$: on each integer vector the coordinate inclusion is exactly $n_i1_F$, also after profinite base change. It preserves the unit and every ordered cup product. Therefore $b\chi_L$ and $\chi_D$ agree on every finite-sum inclusion, including $I=\varnothing$, and hence agree as derived morphisms. Thus $b=\chi_D\chi_L^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. This checks the canonical arrow, rather than choosing an unspecified isomorphism between its endpoints.

proof.text: Choose an $E$-basis $w_1,\ldots,w_n$ of $W$. The coordinate map $W\cong E^n$ and its inverse are continuous by [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous], since the finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is complete and nontrivially valued and the source spaces are finite-dimensional Hausdorff spaces. The induced $F$-linear coordinates identify $F\otimes_EW$ with $F^n$ homeomorphically for the stipulated product norm topology. Concretely the inverse is $(c_j)\mapsto\sum_jc_j\otimes w_j$; changes of basis and their inverses are finite matrices, whose entries act continuously on $F$, so no completeness of $F$ is required. Applying these coordinates pointwise identifies $W_F(S)$ with $C(S,F)^n$, naturally in $S$, $R(S)$-linearly and equivariantly for the trivial $L$- and $D$-actions. This is an isomorphism $W_F\cong R^{\oplus n}$ in both action categories.

proof.text: The derived invariant functors are additive and $b_\iota$ is natural by [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Under the finite-biproduct identifications, naturality with each inclusion and projection says that $b_\iota(R^{\oplus n})$ has the scalar map $b$ on every diagonal component and zero off the diagonal. Its inverse has $b^{-1}$ on every diagonal component. Naturality with the realization isomorphism of step 3 therefore proves invertibility of $b_F(W)$. If $n=0$, additivity makes both derived objects zero and their unique map invertible. If $r=0$, the calculus identifies restriction between the two trivial groups with the identity. These arguments apply separately to $F=E$ and the prescribed norm-topological $F=\Omega$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q09-d614330b5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, the four cited statements, blueprint main-20261015 sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images.proof paragraph (3) and the parent. The delivery is one commit containing the item and its report, with no new nodes and no tool_uses. Statement, stmt_deps and blueprint are byte-identical to live, where the item is still unsplit (not superseded). proof_deps equals the union of the uses, there is no cycle and nothing cites SGA. Step 1: the two exterior statements are used only as statements; both specify the actual maps chi_L and chi_D on the same zero-differential source oplus_I R[-|I|]. Step 2: the calculus gives b[a_i]=[a_i o iota], and a_i o iota is n -> n_i 1_F, which is exactly d_i. Restriction preserves the unit and ordered cups, so b chi_L = chi_D on every summand of the finite biproduct, and b = chi_D chi_L^{-1} is invertible. This proves the canonical arrow itself is an isomorphism, not just that some isomorphism exists. Step 3: E is complete and nontrivially valued and W is normed and finite-dimensional, so the Mathlib leaf applies. Changes of basis are E-matrices, so no completeness of Omega is needed, and C(S,F^n)=C(S,F)^n. Step 4: additivity and naturality give diag(b) on R^n. W=0 gives zero objects and r=0 is the identity clause. Small cases r=0,1,2, W=0 and dim W=1 are consistent. Searching the DAG found no node stating the same comparison; the item is strictly smaller than the parent. Batch-5 finding: both exterior citations reach lem-pod-derived-exact-square-composition only through condensed-derived-restriction-calculus, interchange and kflat-scalar-normalization. That node is a generic pasting identity for derived functors (Stacks 05S7/014F) and is not part of the proof of the trace formula or of Poincare duality, so both citations are accepted.
